title: Normalized derived pullback of a strict coefficient reduction tower
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with a specified ring isomorphism $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Module pullback $F=f^*$ is exact and left adjoint to module direct image $G=f_*$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the ringed-topos convention [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$.
Let $Q_{Y,\bullet}$ be a strict tower of commutative $R_Y$-algebra sheaves with unital algebra transitions, and put $Q_{X,\bullet}=FQ_{Y,\bullet}$ with pulled-back structure maps. Write $\Delta_T$ for constant towers and $F^{\rm Tow}$ for exact termwise pullback. Set $B_T(K)=\Delta_TK\otimes^L_{\Delta_TR_T}Q_{T,\bullet}$ in the derived category of strict towers, equivalently the left derived functor of $P\mapsto(P\otimes_{R_T}Q_{T,n})_n$, with levels restricted to $R_T$. Its augmentation $i_{T,K}:\Delta_TK\to B_T(K)$ is induced by $R_T\to Q_{T,n}$.
There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\tau_K:F^{\rm Tow}B_Y(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X(FK)$$
whose component on every flat-term K-flat representative is the ordinary tensor/pullback comparison, conjugated by the universal reduction counits. The ordinary comparison is the inverse scalar-extension mate of the restriction/pullback comparison: on inverse-image pure tensors it sends $F(x\otimes q)$ to $F(x)\otimes F(q)$. It commutes with all coefficient transitions and satisfies $\tau_K F^{\rm Tow}(i_{Y,K})=i_{X,FK}$ under $F^{\rm Tow}\Delta_Y=\Delta_XF$. Its evaluations are the representative-normalized derived tensor/pullback comparisons. No perfectness or completeness is assumed.

proof.text: Resolve each complex by a flat-term K-flat complex. To show tensor with any fixed complex preserves a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes, resolve that fixed complex by a K-flat complex too. Tensoring the two resolution maps with either K-flat input gives quasi-isomorphisms; the tensor naturality square and two-out-of-three give the required map. For a module placed in degree zero, the single-complex tensor is naturally termwise tensor. Quasi-isomorphisms of tower complexes are detected by evaluation, so the strict reduction functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms between the chosen representatives.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YT: K-flat resolutions and invariance of tensor under quasi-isomorphisms

proof.text: Apply the resolving-class left-derived criterion to the additive reduction functor on homotopy categories. Precomposing its pointwise universal counit with the full homotopy quotient and inserting the quotient/localization factors gives a universal cochain counit, invertible on every good representative. Use its left-derived universal property to lift the coefficient-unit augmentation from the exact constant-tower functor. The universal factorization equation proves the required augmentation normalization. Apply this construction independently on both ringed sites.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes; universal counit and full homotopy-quotient transfer

proof.text: The Comparison argument supplies the ordinary natural tensor isomorphism and its generalized pure-tensor equation. Apply its inverse and the isomorphism identities to prove the required inverse pure normalization. The normalized moduleUnit supplies the right-unit equation. Naturality in each coefficient-unit map, followed by cancellation of the unit isomorphisms, gives compatibility of the ordinary strict-tower comparison with augmentation. Naturality in both module arguments already retains coefficient transitions and complex differentials.

source.place: Tags 03CZ and 03EL: tensor-unit normalization and natural tensor pullback comparison

proof.text: Restriction from derived objects to good complex representatives is fully faithful: restrict the homotopy localization to the resolving full subcategory, and then precompose with the full, essentially surjective quotient from good complexes. Ringed pullback preserves flat-term K-flat representatives. On the good subcategory, compose the first model counit, the exact pullback localization factor, and the ordinary tensor comparison to form a natural isomorphism a. Compose the exact localization factor and the second model counit to form b. Fully faithful restriction lifts a followed by b inverse to a derived natural isomorphism. Its image equation is exactly IsNormalized. Cancellation of b and faithfulness give uniqueness.

source.place: Tags 0G7E, 06YY and 07A4; descent through the resolving localization

proof.text: Check derived augmentation compatibility after restriction to good representatives and cancel the second computing counit together with the exact pullback factor. Substitute the comparison normalization and the two model augmentation equations. Naturality of exact-localization factors and the ordinary augmentation equality reduce the result to compatibility of constantDerivedSquare with those factors. The latter follows from the composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations for exact derived functors. Fully faithful restriction proves augmentation compatibility on all derived objects.

source.place: Tag 06YY, normalized counit computation; sites-modules.tex Tags 03CZ and 03EL

proof.text: For any universal computing cochain counit, transfer to a right Kan extension on homotopy categories. Naturality and invertibility on good representatives show that its ordinary homotopy functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms between such representatives. The resolving criterion makes the associated pro-diagrams essentially constant, so this Kan extension is absolute. Postcomposition by derived evaluation therefore preserves its universal property. Transfer back through the homotopy quotient and insert the exact evaluation localization factor; the resulting natural transformation is precisely evaluationCounit. This proves the two families of left-derived universal properties without imposing boundedness or flatness of coefficient levels.
